title: Technical Success Manager-AMS
description:

• You are a high-trust collaborator. You are ambitious for the team, not just yourself. You embrace our challenge culture by giving and receiving ongoing feedback-knowing that candor delivered with clarity and respect is the truest form of teamwork and the fastest way to earn trust.

• You are a learner. You have a true growth mindset and are obsessed with your own development, actively seeking feedback to become a better partner and a stronger teammate. You love what you do and you do it with purpose.

What We’re Looking for (Minimum Qualifications)

title: Software engineer, cloud infrastructure
description:
ABOUT WATERSHED

Watershed https://watershed.com/ is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

THE ROLE

Watershed’s Cloud Infrastructure team builds and operates the foundational systems that power our product and help every engineer ship safely and efficiently. We own core compute, databases, networking, deployments, and observability, with a focus on production reliability, predictable infrastructure costs, security, and a low-toil developer experience.

Our work spans both operational excellence and high-leverage platform improvements. Current areas of investment include: upgrading our networking architecture, improving the usability of test environments and deployment systems, evolving our observability toolkit, hardening Watershed’s AI infrastructure as our AI product suite grows, and supporting agentic engineering workflows.

YOU WILL

- Design, build, and operate reliable cloud infrastructure that powers all of Watershed (across compute, databases, networking, deployment systems, and observability)

- Contribute to technical planning, design reviews, team processes, and a culture of thoughtful, high-impact development

- Collaborate with product engineers (our internal customers) to understand their needs and provide high-leverage infrastructure primitives that help them move faster, safely

- Strengthen Watershed’s cloud security in partnership with our Security and Compliance functions, and drive infrastructure cost efficiency in collaboration with our Finance team

- Participate in the team’s 24/7 on-call rotation and help turn operational lessons into lasting improvements

YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF

- You have 2-5 years of software and/or infrastructure engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience

- You have hands-on experience in some of these areas: Kubernetes, Terraform / infrastructure as code, CI/CD, networking, relational databases, observability, reliability, or cloud security. Experience with a major cloud provider is a must; experience with GCP is helpful, but not required

- You enjoy the challenge of building the appropriate level of tooling for the stage and arc of the company, in particular being on the front lines of supporting AI infrastructure and agentic products

- You enjoy building enabling systems that help other engineers deliver excellent customer outcomes

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.

What’s the interview process like?

It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.

title: Financial Systems Engineer

As a Financial Systems Engineer, you will design, build, and operate the financial systems and integrations that support critical accounting processes across Oracle Fusion Cloud and OpenAI’s broader finance technology ecosystem. You’ll partner with Corporate Accounting, Accounts Payable, Revenue Accounting, Supply Chain, Engineering, Data, Tax, and other cross-functional teams to deliver reliable, scalable, and auditable solutions.

This role requires deep Oracle Financials expertise, strong accounting process knowledge, and an engineering mindset. You will work across corporate accounting processes including equity, payroll, accruals, leases, mergers and acquisitions, intercompany, and close; transform Accounts Payable processes; and design solutions for complex supply chain accounting, cost accounting, ASC 606 revenue recognition, and compute and data-center accounting. You’ll help redefine how finance teams work by applying automation, AI, and agentic approaches to reduce manual effort, strengthen controls, and accelerate accounting and close processes.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

title: Founding Creative Director, Interactive & AI
description:
About Lynton

Lynton spent 16 years as a HubSpot partner, delivering 2,000+ projects across 50+ industries. We know SaaS and agency work from the inside. When we saw what was coming with AI, we left HubSpot to build what comes next.
We build and run AI-native growth systems for mid-market companies: websites built to be measured, an open-source stack that replaces legacy software, and AI agents that run marketing, sales, and operations. The client owns the infrastructure, we operate the agents, and the whole system has to show what it produces in revenue.
If this role sounds like a perfect fit for you, skip ahead to apply directly on our website. We prioritize candidates who apply directly on our site.

The opportunity

Most agencies have added AI to their production line and kept the creative process they had ten years ago. We started over. AI coding agents build our websites. Our imagery comes from image and video models we direct. The interactive work that used to need a studio and a six-figure budget is now something a small team can ship in weeks.

What that makes possible depends on taste. Anyone can generate a thousand images. Very few people can pick the right one, fix what's wrong with it, and make it move in a way that serves the page's argument. That's the job.

As our founding creative director, you own the creative and communication strategy for every website and campaign Lynton ships, both ours and our clients'. You decide what a page says and how it looks. You design how it moves. You make or direct every image, illustration, animation, and film on it. Some weeks you're writing the headline. Other weeks you're lighting a scene in Blender, or telling a client their brand deserves better than stock photography.

The agency is one part of what we're building. Lynton is also a launchpad for new products, services, and companies we incubate from inside, and with your help we'll take each of them to market.

What you'll own

•
Creative and communication strategy. Own the messaging and visual system for every site and campaign. That covers positioning, page structure, headlines, body copy, the design language, and the design tokens that encode it. You write copy yourself and edit everything that ships, so the words and pictures come from one point of view.

•
Interactive experience design. Design how every page moves and responds, including SVG and CSS animation, scroll-driven storytelling, micro-interactions, and real-time 3D. You storyboard it, prototype it, and direct the build. When getting into the timeline yourself is faster than explaining, you do that.

•
3D and real-time scenes. Model, light, and art-direct scenes in Blender, then bring them to the browser with Three.js and WebGL. You set the bar for when a page earns real-time 3D and when a lighter technique tells the story better.

•
Generated photography and illustration. Build and run the image pipeline. You'll art-direct photography and illustration with image models, keep one style consistent across a whole site or campaign, and retouch what the model gets wrong. You'll also animate stills with video models. You set the house rules on style, consistency, and licensing.

•
Video and motion graphics. Produce product films, launch and explainer videos, social cuts, and motion graphics. Use generative video, compositing, and traditional motion tools in whatever mix gets the best result.

•
Campaign creative. Own launches and email campaigns end to end: concept, copy, landing pages, imagery, and video. A campaign should read as one idea from the inbox to the page.

•
New products, services, and brands. Lead the creative for every launch we incubate: the name and identity, the positioning and story, and the site and campaign it goes to market with.

•
Creative oversight on every engagement. You review and sign off on all creative the agency ships. You're the reason a Lynton site looks and reads like one, and the reason no client site looks like a template.

title: AI Specialist
description:
We’re Capital on Tap 👋
💳 Capital on Tap started because small businesses were underserved. Big banks were slow, their products weren't fit for purpose, and small business owners often couldn't access what they needed. We set out to fix that.

Today we're a financial platform - not just a credit card company. We offer a best-in-class business credit card, SME-focused spend management platform, a savings product that hit £1 billion in funds within its first year, and a growing suite of tools and financial products that make running a small business easier. 

1,000+ employees, £20bn in annual card spend, 200,000+ customers, 17,000+ Trustpilot reviews averaging 4.7 stars, and we're profitable. We’ve done a pretty good job so far, but we’re just getting started! 

📍 London (Moorgate) | 🏢 3 Days in Office

The Role

Most companies talk about AI. We're building the infrastructure to make it stick. This role exists to close the gap between AI's potential and what our teams actually use every day.

You'll embed with a team, find the highest-impact opportunities, build the tools that solve them, and train the team to run them long after you've moved on. This isn't a research or strategy role. You'll be shipping automations, MCPs, plugins, agentic workflows, and the training that goes with them. You'll be measured on impact and weekly active users, not on launches or tools rolled out. If you'd rather be doing than advising, this is for you.

What You’ll Be Doing 

•
Analyse where AI can move the needle most. Map a team's processes end-to-end before proposing a single tool, and prioritise the workflows where AI can take real cost, time, or rework off the table.

•
Build the right stack for the problem - production-grade agentic workflows that bridge LLMs, internal APIs, and case management tools, plus MCPs, Claude skills and plugins, n8n automations, and integrations with internal systems. You build it, debug it in production, and iterate live with users sitting next to you.

•
Train the people who'll use it. Run hands-on sessions, write documentation people actually read, and coach AI champions inside every team you work with so they're self-sufficient before you move on.

•
Roll out and measure. Active automations running unsupervised matter more than trainings delivered or pilots launched. Track weekly active AI users and impact per team, intervene when usage drops, and keep iterating until AI is part of how the team works.

•
Maintain Capital on Tap's AI playbook. Document repeatable patterns, package them as reusable skills and templates, and make every engagement start faster than the last.

•
Partner with senior stakeholders to decide where to point next, and what good looks like before you start.

We’re Looking For 

•
Deployed AI tools in environments where downtime, errors, or rework have real cost - not sandbox experimentation.

•
Hands-on, proven experience with Claude, Cursor, n8n, Zapier, or similar in a real business context.

•
Technical fluency across low-code/no-code tools, APIs, MCPs, and integrations; comfortable in SQL and familiar with BI tooling.

•
2-5 years in product ops, operations, strategy, technical programme management, internal consulting, or a similar hands-on role.

•
Strong communicator. You can run a workshop that lands, write documentation people actually read, and translate jargon for any audience.

•
Comfortable with ambiguity. You diagnose fast, prioritise ruthlessly, and ship a working v1 inside a week even when the team you're working with isn't yet sure what they want.

•
High ownership. You figure out what needs doing and do it, without waiting to be told.

Even if you don’t have all of the necessary skills, we still encourage you to apply.

Diversity & Inclusion  🌈

We welcome, consider and encourage applications from anyone who shares our commitment to inclusivity. Join us in creating a space where authenticity thrives, and everyone can do their best work.

What You’ll Do

During the task, you will:

•
Review the checkout experience, including subscription pricing and applicable Utility Users Tax (UUT) calculations.

title: Application Security Consultant*
description:
Was du bei uns bewegen kannst
Sichere Software-Architekturen und Kulturen etablieren: Du begleitest und berätst unsere Kunden ganzheitlich rund um das Thema Application Security. Dabei baust du robuste Secure-SDLC- sowie Vulnerability-Management-Prozesse auf und verankerst präventive Sicherheitsmaßnahmen fest im Entwicklungszyklus.
Wissen vermitteln & Befähigung vorantreiben: Mit interaktiven Formaten wie Threat-Modeling-Workshops, GAP-Analysen, Trainings (z. B. zu Web Security oder dem Cyber Resilience Act) und der Etablierung von Security-Champions-Programmen befähigst du Teams, Security nachhaltig in ihren Alltag zu integrieren.
Gestaltungskraft & Portfolio-Entwicklung: Nach innen bietet dir die Rolle großen Gestaltungsspielraum. Gemeinsam mit dem Team treibst du in einer CoP (inoCircle) die strategische Ausrichtung unseres Leistungsportfolios aktiv mit voran. Zudem konzipierst du eigene Trainingsangebote und gestaltest zukunftsfähige Beratungsprodukte mit.
Außenwirksamkeit & Community-Engagement: Als Expert:in für Application Security vertrittst du inovex nach außen. Durch Vorträge auf Konferenzen oder Meetups und Beiträge auf LinkedIn teilst du dein Wissen, prägst Technologietrends und stärkst unsere Sichtbarkeit in der Community.
Hands-on-Expertise & technische Tiefe: In Security Reviews spürst du Schwachstellen gezielt auf und setzt dabei Werkzeuge wie SAST, DAST und SCA ein. Die Ergebnisse priorisierst du gemeinsam mit den Entwicklungsteams. Auch die Software Supply Chain (von Dependencies bis zur SBOM) hast du fest im Blick und bewertest KI- und LLM-Anwendungen entlang der OWASP Top 10 for LLM.
Requirements
Wer gut zu uns passen würde
Fundiertes Security-Know-how : Deine Basis ist ein abgeschlossenes Studium (Master/Bachelor oder Promotion) in Informatik, Cyber Security oder einem vergleichbaren Studiengang. Alternativ hast du dir gleichwertige tiefgehende Praxiserfahrung erarbeitet. Zudem bringst du mehrjährige Erfahrung in der IT-Sicherheit und Softwareentwicklung mit.
Breite Tech-Expertise mit klaren Schwerpunkten: Ein breiter Technologiemix schreckt dich nicht ab. Idealerweise vereinst du dein tiefes Security-Wissen mit zwei bis drei weiteren Standbeinen - zum Beispiel Fullstack Development, Cloud-Infrastrukturen, Data Engineering oder KI.
Praxisnahe Beratung & Zertifizierungen: Ein pragmatischer Blick auf Security-Compliance (z. B. CRA) zeichnet dich ebenso aus wie die Fähigkeit, komplexe Sicherheitskonzepte verständlich zu vermitteln. Zertifizierungen (z. B. CSSLP) oder Know-how im Bereich AI / LLM Security sind ein klares Plus.
Eigeninitiative & Beratungspersönlichkeit: Für dich ist es selbstverständlich, über den Tellerrand hinauszudenken. Beim Kunden bringst du deine eigene Perspektive und Expertise gewinnbringend ein und überzeugst Stakeholder durch fachliche Exzellenz, Empathie sowie lösungsorientierte Kommunikation.
Sprachkompetenz: Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse sind Voraussetzung (mind. Level C1), gute Englischkenntnisse runden dein Profil ab.

Job Title: In-Home Physician Full Time - Medford

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Seniority Level:
We’re building a world of health around every individual - shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger - helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Full Time Physician to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.
You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.
Job highlights
The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.
In this role, you will:

• Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

• Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

• Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

• Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

• Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.
Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD
The primary care physician gets a snapshot of a person in an office setting, but with Signify Health, we see things like the number of steps to enter their home, the state of disrepair those steps may be in, and the person’s ability to function comfortably and with ease in their own home. We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD
Full-time employees qualify for our comprehensive benefits package, including:

• Health, dental and vision insurance

• Paid time off

• Annual CEU allowance

• 401K

• Supplies and other perks

• Malpractice coverage

Required & Preferred Qualifications (MDs and DOs)

• Active, unrestricted license(s) in coverage area(s)

• Multi-state licenses (preferred)

title: Senior / Principal Materials Scientist, AI Safety
locationText: Cambridge, MA USA; London, UK; San Francisco, CA USA
description:
Your Impact at LILA

We're building a talent-dense, high-agency AI safety team at Lila that will engage all core teams within the organization (science, model training, lab integration, etc.), to identify and mitigate risks from scientific superintelligence while retaining the core scientific discovery capabilities of the stack. The initial focus of this team will be to build and implement a bespoke safety strategy for Lila, tailored to its specific goals and deployment strategies. This will involve technical safety strategy development, broader ecosystem engagement, safety-focused evaluations, safety systems to mitigate risks, and a research agenda that explores longer-term needs such as oversight of superintelligent scientific systems.

We are seeking a materials scientist to map risk across the material sciences domain: you will connect deep materials expertise with dual-use risk assessment to help safeguard increasingly capable scientific AI. You will investigate how advances in materials research could change harmful capabilities, including established and emerging threats.

What You'll Be Building

• Map misuse risks by connecting material properties, processing and functional performance (across a range of materials domains) to harmful applications, including emerging or overlooked uses of scientific advances.

• Assess how physical feasibility, processing complexity, manufacturing requirements and actors' resources affect the plausibility and likelihood of misuse, including which constraints AI could change.

• Distinguish established capabilities, plausible future developments and weakly supported hypotheses, revising assessments as evidence changes across models, tools and automated laboratories.

• Identify gaps in expertise, commission targeted scientific input with the expert-program team, and integrate specialist findings into a coherent assessment of the risk landscape.

• Translate dual-use judgments into policy boundaries, evaluation priorities and mitigation requirements that support beneficial materials research.

• Work with threat modelers, evaluation researchers and engineering and experimental colleagues to assess capabilities, interpret red-team findings and evaluate safeguards.

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Deep expertise (a PhD, or comparable experience) in materials science or a closely related discipline, with a strong grasp of the relationships between structure, properties, processing and applications. Relevant backgrounds include particulate, porous and formulated systems; and structural and functional materials, including thin films, electrochemical materials and metals and alloys.

• Substantive experience assessing dual-use risks in a relevant area, with a strong understanding of harmful applications such as nuclear proliferation, radiological misuse, weapons-related capabilities (e.g. energetics) or other consequential materials risks.

• Sound judgment about physical possibility, practical feasibility and uncertainty, together with the ability to investigate risks beyond your immediate specialism.

• The ability to identify appropriate specialists, evaluate technical evidence and synthesize contributions across scientific and security disciplines.

• Clear scientific communication, independent research judgment and an ability to collaborate across science, engineering and policy.

Bonus Points For

• Prior experience applying materials or related physical-science expertise to AI safety through one or more of: threat analysis, evaluations or red teaming, or mitigation design.

• Experience commissioning specialist research or assessing emerging technologies across disciplinary boundaries.

• Experience with computational materials science, advanced manufacturing or automated synthesis and characterization.

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

The Learning Designer role at Valenture Institute is primarily responsible for designing, developing and quality assuring secondary school course content and learning activities for online delivery, in line with curriculum requirements, SACAI requirements and Valenture’s internal learning design standards. The incumbent is responsible for delivering high-quality course content within agreed scope and timelines, and for ensuring that their work meets the required curriculum, quality and learning design standards.
Key responsibilities
Curriculum, Learning & Assessment Design

• Use the relevant curriculum, subject and assessment requirements to ensure that course content is accurate, appropriately scoped and aligned to the required NSC and SACAI standards.

• Conduct planning and analysis in subject area to recommend appropriate design solutions and strategies for online delivery.

• Use Valenture’s learning management system and available learning technologies to make appropriate design decisions for online learning.

• Design appropriate formative learning, practice and mastery activities that help learners build and demonstrate understanding as they progress through the course.

• Design and develop curriculum-aligned summative assessments, including the associated marking guidelines and assessment materials, in accordance with CAPS, NSC, SACAI and Valenture assessment requirements.

Content development & production

• Develop and adapt curriculum-aligned source material into engaging, pedagogically sound online learning experiences using Valenture’s approved development tools and formats.

• Research and source appropriate reference materials to support course development.

• Collaborate with relevant Product, Learning Technology and production specialists to create supporting media and interactive learning elements where required.

• Develop educational content from scratch, making use of various sources, into a richly augmented format that meets online delivery objectives.

• Perform auxiliary tasks, including, but not limited to briefing in graphics, and tracking the use of external assets.

• Develop content in accordance with Valenture’s agreed learning design principles, development processes, templates, SOPs and quality standards.

Quality Assurance & Continuous Improvement

• Review and quality assure their own work against agreed curriculum, learning design and quality requirements before submission for review.

• Participate in peer review and quality assurance activities across courses, and implement feedback arising from review.Perform peer reviews across subjects and qualifications.

• Review the effectiveness of learning design approaches and contribute to ongoing improvements to course content.

• Contribute feedback and recommendations on Learning Design processes and ways of working.

Delivery & Collaboration

• Manage assigned development work against agreed timelines, proactively communicating progress, blockers and delivery risks to the Senior Learning Designer.

• Collaborate effectively with the Senior Learning Designer, other Learning Designers and relevant Product, Learning Technology and operational stakeholders.

• Participate in agreed team rhythms, reviews and development planning activities.

Key requirements

• A relevant teaching qualification, with appropriate subject specialisation for the subject being developed.

• Demonstrated knowledge of the CAPS curriculum and experience teaching or developing learning material in the relevant subject and phase.

• Experience in learning design, curriculum development or the development of high-quality digital learning content is advantageous.

• Experience in the EdTech field is advantageous

• Knowledge of digital learning principles and practices will be advantageous

• Meticulous attention to detail and accuracy

• Ability to communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders, and build collaborative work relationships

title: Policy Advisor, Fossil Fuel Transition
description:
About Us
The International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today's greatest sustainable development challenges. We combine deep expertise across critical policy areas with a collaborative approach to research, advice, and hands-on support that delivers real-world results. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, we are a diverse team of over 300 experts working from offices in Canada and Switzerland as well as other locations around the world. Our research and policy advice help governments, businesses, communities, and civil society make better decisions. Our international Energy Program works with partners across countries and disciplines.
We are currently looking for a Policy Advisor, Fossil Fuel Transition, to work within the IISD Energy Program.
About the Position
The Policy Advisor, Fossil Fuel Transition, will work within IISD’s International Strategy team, helping governments and partners advance a Paris-aligned, just, orderly and equitable transition away from fossil fuel production and consumption, including reform of fossil fuel subsidies and public finance. We recognize the difficult choices facing fossil-fuel-dependent economies: protecting public revenues, energy security, jobs, and affordability while building more resilient and diversified economies. The role involves close collaboration with government counterparts, particularly in the Global South, and with researchers, intergovernmental organizations, and civil society, as well as other teams within IISD’s 50-staff Energy Program and other Institute programs.
The Policy Advisor will help design and implement applied research, policy advice, and technical assistance for countries seeking practical transition pathways. For example, the work may examine the effects of changing fossil fuel revenues on government budgets, assess subsidy reform options, or help translate national and international transition commitments into implementable measures. Key responsibilities include
Responsibilities

• Leading policy-oriented research and analysis on fossil fuel transitions, public financial flows, macroeconomic and fiscal risks, subsidies, energy security and economic diversification; translating evidence into actionable options for decision-makers.

• Designing and managing assigned workstreams and outputs, with clear workplans, responsibilities, quality checks, and milestones; coordinating partners; and contributing to reporting and budget management alongside financial project managers.

• Building trusted relationships with government counterparts, especially in fossil fuel-dependent economies, as well as knowledge organizations, civil society networks and intergovernmental partners; adapting support to country needs and available evidence.

• Supporting the development of more junior colleagues through clear task briefs, constructive feedback, peer review, and learning by doing.

• Contributing to focused funding proposals and partner engagement that build on demonstrated demand and the team’s existing expertise.

• Working with IISD Communications early in the process to turn research into clear, useful messages and products for intended audiences.

About the Successful Applicant
We are looking for a thoughtful, self-directed policy professional who combines analytical rigour with practical judgement and reliable delivery. The successful applicant can turn a complex policy question into a workable plan, communicate trade-offs clearly, and work constructively with colleagues across disciplines and time zones. They will understand that fossil fuel-dependent countries face real fiscal, political, and development constraints and will seek credible, country-owned transition solutions rather than one-size-fits-all prescriptions. This is a hands-on role with opportunities to take growing ownership and help develop colleagues.

title: Fortinet Network Security Engineer - North Central region
description:
GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation’s top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

General Description
We are looking for a skilled Fortinet Network Security Engineer to support our Network Security & PKI Practice in designing, implementing, and managing Fortinet based security solutions for our managed service and consulting clients. This role will engage in the development of resilient firewall, VPN, and SD-WAN architectures while providing “Wow Them” service to clients and/or internal customers or co-workers.
The Fortinet Network Security Engineer will be required to demonstrate strong troubleshooting, communication, and documentation skills, lead by influence, and strong business/financial acumen to drive the use of progressive network security programs that will align the delivery with business objectives and priorities.
About the Network Security & PKI Practice - North Central region
The Network Security & PKI Practice is responsible for designing, deploying, and operating the network security and encryption technologies that protect our clients’ environments. We deliver firewall, secure connectivity, segmentation, and public key infrastructure solutions across the organization and for our managed service and consulting clients.
Our team of network security engineers, consultants, and architects focuses on next generation firewalls, SD-WAN, secure remote access, and zero trust architecture across leading vendor platforms. We partner with client stakeholders, delivery teams, and internal practices to translate security requirements into reliable, well documented outcomes.
Current initiatives and areas of focus include:

• Delivering managed Fortinet security services across multi-tenant, multi-client environments

• Advancing zero trust architecture and network segmentation for clients in regulated industries

• Standardizing repeatable, well documented deployment and operational practices

Roles and Responsibilities:

• Design, implement, and support network security solutions using Fortinet technologies (FortiGate, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiSwitch).

• Configure and manage firewall policies, VPNs (IPSec/SSL), SD-WAN, and UTM features.

• Utilize FortiManager for centralized management and policy deployment across multiple FortiGate devices.

• Use FortiAnalyzer for event correlation, log analysis, and reporting.

• Perform regular health checks, upgrades, and policy audits on Fortinet equipment.

• Support networking infrastructure, including switching, VLANs, static and dynamic routing (OSPF, BGP), and subnetting.

• Troubleshoot network and security issues across multiple clients or environments.

• Collaborate with clients and internal teams to recommend and implement security best practices.

• Document configurations, diagrams, and standard operating procedures.

Required Experience and Education:

• 2+ years of hands-on experience with Fortinet security technologies (FortiGate, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiSwitch).

• Solid understanding of core networking concepts: subnetting, NAT, routing protocols (OSPF, BGP), switching, and VLANs.

• Experience with firewall policy creation, security profiles, and VPN configurations.

• Strong troubleshooting, analytical, written, and verbal communication skills.

• Basic Fortinet certification required prior to hire (NSE 4 or higher preferred).

• Embraces emerging technologies, including AI tools, to work smarter, solve problems, and drive better business outcomes.

Preferred Experience and Education

• Experience with multi-tenant firewall environments and managing clients in regulated industries

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing - and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. An ideal candidate has :

TeccWeb is an Epicor Service Partner specializing in the implementation and optimization of Epicor ERP solutions for mid-market companies worldwide. With our diverse skill set and collaborative approach, we help clients solve complex business challenges and maximize the value of their ERP systems. Our success is built on strong, long-term partnerships with our clients.
We are seeking an Epicor Financial Implementation Consultant to guide our clients through their ERP transformations. In this role, you will bridge the gap between complex manufacturing accounting workflows and Epicor technology. You will lead client-facing workshops, configure financial modules, and ensure successful go-lives.
Key Responsibilities

• Client Advisory & Workshop Facilitation: Lead discovery sessions, gather business requirements, map current-to-future state processes, and advise clients on industry best practices.

• Full-Lifecycle Implementation: Actively participate in all project phases for Epicor Financial modules-from system design and configuration to data migration, UAT testing, user training, and post-go-live support.

• Experience in an external consulting firm or as a dedicated internal ERP Lead/Super User.

What we offer

• Fully remote position in Canada or USA (no relocation required). California excluded.

• Competitive salary, based on experience.

• Opportunities for career growth and ongoing training.

• Join TeccWeb and be part of a team of experts working on exciting projects!

title: Payment Integrity Nurse Reviewer- Hospital Claims
description:
We are seeking an experienced Senior Claims Analyst with deep expertise in hospital claims adjudication, stop loss reporting, high-cost/catastrophic claims, and DRG (Diagnosis-Related Group) reimbursement methodology. This individual will analyze itemized hospital bills and claims data to identify billing errors, coding discrepancies, DRG misassignments, and other overpayment opportunities, then work directly with claims administrators on behalf of our ASO clients to secure claim adjustments, recoveries, and repricing.
This is a highly analytical, client-facing role requiring both technical claims expertise and strong negotiation/communication skills.
This is a remote role.
Key Responsibilities
Claims Analysis & Review

• Perform detailed audits of hospital and facility claims, including itemized bills, UB-04 claim forms, medical records, and remittance advices, to validate billing accuracy.

• Analyze DRG assignments and coding to identify DRG upcoding, unbundling, duplicate billing, and other irregularities that affect reimbursement.

• Review high-cost and catastrophic claims (typically $100K+) to identify overpayments, contract misapplication, and opportunities for negotiated adjustments.

• Evaluate claims against plan documents, provider contracts, reference-based pricing methodologies, and CMS guidelines to determine appropriate reimbursement.

Stop Loss & High-Cost Claims Expertise

• Understand and apply stop loss (specific and aggregate) provisions, laser terms, and reporting requirements as they relate to claim adjustments and client financial exposure.

• Coordinate with stop loss carriers and reinsurers as needed to ensure adjustments and recoveries are properly reflected in stop loss reimbursement calculations.

• Identify claims nearing or exceeding specific deductible thresholds and prioritize review accordingly.

Client Advocacy & Claims Administrator Negotiation

• Serve as the subject matter expert and advocate on behalf of ASO clients in disputes with claims administrators (TPAs) and carriers regarding claim payment accuracy.

• Prepare clear, well-documented findings packages (clinical, contractual, and coding rationale) to support requested claim adjustments and appeals.

• Lead or support negotiations with claims administrators to reach adjusted payment resolutions.

• Track disputes through resolution, escalating unresolved cases appropriately and maintaining strong working relationships with TPA claims and provider relations teams.

Data & Reporting

• Analyze large claims data sets to identify trends, outlier claims, and systemic overpayment patterns across client populations.

• Build and maintain claim tracking logs, savings reports, and client-facing summaries of identified and recovered savings.

• Partner with internal data/analytics teams to refine claim-flagging logic and improve identification of high-value review opportunities.

Required Qualifications

• Hospital/Surgical/ICU Nursing background (RN) and clinical coding background for clinical validation of DRG and medical necessity issues.

• 5+ years of experience in hospital claims analysis, medical bill review, claims auditing, or payment integrity, with direct exposure to self-funded/ASO plans.

• Strong working knowledge of DRG methodology (MS-DRG/APR-DRG), UB-04 billing, ICD-10-CM/PCS, CPT/HCPCS coding, and hospital chargemaster structures.

• Demonstrated understanding of stop loss insurance, including specific/aggregate deductibles, laser provisions, and how claim adjustments impact stop loss reimbursement.

• Experience analyzing high-cost/catastrophic claims and identifying overpayment or billing error patterns.

• Prior experience interacting with or negotiating against TPAs, insurance carriers, or claims administrators on disputed claims.

title: KYC产品经理
description:
• 这个职位为何存在？它解决什么问题？我们为什么现在需要它？

KYC 是用户准入的第一道门，直接影响转化率、欺诈与合规成本。该岗位存在的意义是：把「能过审」变成「又好又快又准」的产品体验，用指标体系定位链路断点，并用竞品与技术扫描保持方案不过时。现在需要它，是因为业务增长与审核精度、自动规则、法规解读之间需要专人持续做产品化平衡，而不是靠运营或风控临时补位。

• 核心职责（3-5条）

• 主导 KYC 产品功能设计与体验优化，提升流程转化率与核验准确性。

• 搭建并维护 KYC 数据指标体系，定期采集与分析使用数据，识别并推动解决转化链路中的关键痛点。

• 持续跟踪行业与竞品动态，结构化输出竞品能力、差异点与市场策略，反哺产品路线与优先级。

• 研究并评估新兴 KYC 技术（如 AI 身份识别、区块链数据共享等），判断其适用场景、风险边界与对现有产品的价值，形成可落地的引入或试点建议。

• 理想候选人是什么样的？
熟悉 KYC 全链路语言--从用户填表、证件采集、活体/OCR 到自动审核与人工兜底--并能用数据说话：先定义「哪里漏、哪里卡、哪里误杀」，再改交互与策略。对「秒过」有工程化理解：知道在什么合规与风险边界下追求极致体验，而不是单纯追求表面通过率。习惯主动扫厂商能力与行业方案，比较优劣后能写清楚「我们为什么选 A 不选 B」。能把法规要求读进产品规格里，而不是停留在合规部门的 PPT 上。

• 吸引人的亮点（1-2条）

• 工作直接挂钩 转化率与准确性 等可感知业务结果，改动能快速在数据上验证。

• 可深度接触 AI 身份识别、OCR、自动审核与风控规则 的交叉地带，并参与前沿技术方案的评估与落地路径设计。

description:
ÜBER COSUNO

Die Baubranche ist eine 14-Billionen-Euro-Industrie, die noch immer auf E-Mails, Excel-Tabellen und eingescannten PDFs läuft. Cosuno ersetzt das durch KI. Generalunternehmer schreiben ihre Projekte auf unserer Plattform an mehr als 250.000 Nachunternehmer aus, und unsere agentische KI findet die passenden Firmen, erkennt Auffälligkeiten in Angeboten und vergleicht jeden Preis mit 6,5 Millionen Datenpunkten aus über 136 Milliarden Euro verarbeitetem Angebotsvolumen. Jede Ausschreibung macht die KI klüger. Die Ergebnisse sind messbar: Generalunternehmer senken ihre Kosten um rund 6 %, Nachunternehmer gewinnen 22 % mehr Volumen, und jeder neue Generalunternehmer-Kunde hat sich in diesem Jahr für unser KI-Produkt entschieden. 2019 in Berlin gegründet und von Cherry Ventures und Spark Capital mit über 40 Millionen Euro finanziert, skalieren wir mit diesem Kapital jetzt Sales, Customer Success und Marketing. Und genau hier kommst du ins Spiel.

DIE ROLLE

Du bekommst jede Woche neue Kunden zugewiesen, die sich nicht selbst aktiviert haben, und führst sie durch das Onboarding: Erstkontakt innerhalb weniger Tage, Onboarding-Call per Screenshare, Profil und Suchprofil einrichten, erste Angebote begleiten. Rund 40 Onboardings im Monat, jedes etwa anderthalb Stunden Gesamtaufwand inklusive Vorbereitung und Nachfassen.

Du misst dich nicht am abgehaltenen Call, sondern am Kunden, der danach selbst weitermacht. Dafür verfolgst du die Aktivierungssignale jedes Kunden in Salesforce und greifst nach, wo einer hängen bleibt.

Du bist die Person im Unternehmen, die am häufigsten sieht, wo Neukunden scheitern. Dieses Wissen gibst du strukturiert an Product weiter, damit Tool Tips, Product Tours und Hilfetexte besser werden und mehr Kunden sich selbst aktivieren.

Du berichtest an den Head of Customer Success und arbeitest eng mit dem Sales-Team, das die Kunden abschließt, und mit den Customer Success Managern, die bei Kündigungen übernehmen.

WORAN WIR DICH NACH 12 MONATEN MESSEN

- Mindestens 90 % deiner Kunden sind 30 Tage nach dem Onboarding aktiv - Profil vollständig, Suchprofil eingerichtet, erstes Angebot abgegeben.

- Jeder zugewiesene Kunde hat innerhalb von drei Werktagen von dir gehört.

- Salesforce ist bei dir vollständig: Onboarding-Status, Aktivierungssignale, Hürden - bei jedem Kunden.

WER BEI COSUNO ERFOLGREICH IST

- Ownership. Wenn ein Kunde nach 30 Tagen nicht aktiv ist, fragst du zuerst, was du anders hättest machen können.

- Speed. Du rufst heute an, nicht nächste Woche. Ein Kunde, der drei Wochen wartet, hat Cosuno vergessen.

- Drive. Du hast schon einmal ein Skript, eine Checkliste oder einen Ablauf gebaut, weil der alte nicht funktioniert hat - ohne dass dich jemand gebeten hat.

- Low Ego. Du teilst, was bei dir funktioniert, damit das Team besser wird.

DIESE ROLLE IST FÜR DICH, WENN

- du gern erklärst und dabei merkst, wann dein Gegenüber wirklich verstanden hat - und wann es nur nickt.

- du 40 Gespräche im Monat als Rhythmus empfindest, nicht als Last.

- du nach dem dritten Nichterreichen zum vierten Mal anrufst, zu einer anderen Uhrzeit - unsere Kunden stehen auf der Baustelle.

- du Handwerksbetriebe magst und mit einem Dachdecker genauso sprichst wie mit einer Büroleitung.

DIESE ROLLE IST NICHTS FÜR DICH, WENN

- du Onboarding als Schulung verstehst und nach dem Call abhakst.

- du Tickets abarbeiten willst statt Kunden hinterherzutelefonieren

- du zehn Kunden intensiv betreuen möchtest statt vierzig in die Nutzung zu bringen.

- dich eine Zahl über deinem Schreibtisch stresst statt motiviert.

HARTE ANFORDERUNGEN

- Mindestens 1 Jahr in einer kundennahen Rolle mit Volumen: Onboarding, Customer Support mit Aktivierungsziel, Inside Sales, Kundenservice im B2B.

- Sicher im Erklären von Software per Telefon und Screenshare.

- Strukturiert und CRM-diszipliniert.

- Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau (C2), Englisch gut.

- Berlin oder Bereitschaft zu Bürotagen.

VERGÜTUNG

55.000 € OTE pro Jahr

• Self-directed and comfortable owning a channel without heavy supervision.

title: Payroll Lead
description:
TL;DR:

You will own and shape payroll at Lovable at a point where the model is genuinely open. Today it's outsourced; where it lands, continuing to oversee and approve the work of our service centers, or bringing the whole thing in-house and running it end-to-end, is undecided and yours to figure out. This is a senior, high-ownership role for an AI-pilled, expert Swedish payroll professional who has done this before and wants to build payroll into a tight, automated, reliable machine at one of the fastest-growing AI companies in the world.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we’re looking for

- We're bringing payroll ownership into Finance, and the model is deliberately open: keep it part-outsourced, bring it fully in-house, or land in between, your call to make.

- As our first dedicated Payroll Lead you'll own that model and the build-versus-buy calls, starting in Sweden and potentially scaling to global.

You should have

- Expert, current, hands-on Swedish payroll knowledge: Skatteverket employer reporting (AGI), employer contributions, expert tax / SINK, pensions and benefits, and working knowledge of LAS and BFL

- Proven track record owning payroll that you can point to

- Senior-manager level, with 8+ years of payroll experience

- Genuine appetite to own payroll end-to-end and shape the operating model, including the build-versus-buy decision on what we run in-house versus outsource

- Strong payroll accounting skills: journals, accruals, reconciliations, month-end close, and correct entity and cost-centre coding

- Exposure to equity / share-based compensation payroll and benefit-in-kind taxation

- Comfort with ambiguity and a greenfield remit, and an audit-ready, controls-minded way of working

- Ability to work independently and make decisions without a team behind you yet

- Excellent English communication skills (Swedish a strong plus given the Swedish payroll focus)

Nice to have

- International or multi-entity payroll exposure (UK, US, EOR) is a strong plus and points to the path to global lead

- A deeply AI-pilled way of working: you reach for AI and automation by default and want to build a modern, automated payroll function rather than a manual one

What you’ll do

- Shape and own how payroll is delivered: whether we oversee and approve outsourced service centers, bring payroll fully in-house end-to-end, or a mix, and lead the transition wherever it lands

- Build payroll into a tight, reliable, highly automated operation, with accuracy and control as the standard

- Own payroll accounting: journals, accruals and reconciliations into the GL, and support month-end close

- Drive automation of payroll so recurring work is systematized, not manual

- Own the payroll and tax treatment of equity events (option exercises, secondaries, clawbacks, benefits in kind

title: Principal System Architect
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

 

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

 

Product Architecture & Safety (PAS) defines, governs and validates the system and product architecture of Wayve AI Driver across programs, giving OEMs and partners one technical voice. Our growing system architecture team works across assisted driving through L4 driver-out.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

 

• Own end-to-end system architecture, interface contracts, assumptions of use and decision records.
• Lead technical discussions with OEMs, Tier 1s and partners, aligning internal architecture owners around a common direction.
• Define ECU and sensor requirements, guide system engineers and support integration planning, bring-up, triage and system-level debugging on vehicles and HiL/ViL benches.

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

 

Shape how Wayve AI Driver is deployed across L0-L4, with near-term focus on L3 eyes-off and L4 driver-out. The scope starts where Robotaxi needs are highest and grows with the business.

 

• Translate use cases, ODD and operational constraints into reusable product, system and integration architecture.
• Define sensor and compute topology, vehicle interfaces, safety mechanisms, redundancy, fallback and minimal-risk manoeuvre assumptions with safety engineering.
• Define on-board/off-board architecture for connectivity, remote assistance and operation, and fleet operations, including latency, availability and Wayve/OEM/operator ownership.
• Distinguish core product changes from partner-specific integration so deployment needs strengthen one common architecture.

 

🙌 You should apply if

 

Essential
• Strong experience in system architecture, systems engineering or solution architecture for ADAS / AD, robotics or complex safety-relevant embedded systems.
• Broad understanding across system and vehicle-level architecture, sensors, compute and hardware, embedded software, vehicle integration and safety.
• Experience defining and owning product or integration architecture for complex, cross-functional systems end-to-end.
• Ability to translate high-level product or deployment goals into concrete architectural requirements and trade-offs.
• Experience working across multiple technical domains and aligning different engineering stakeholders.
• Experience leading technical discussions with OEMs, Tier 1s or other external partners.
• Working knowledge of ISO 26262 and ISO 21448 (SOTIF) and how they shape system architecture.
• Strong written and verbal communication, including architecture documents that others build from.
• Hands-on enough to support technical problem-solving, bring-up and integration trade-offs in practice.

 

Desirable
• Experience with L3 eyes-off, L4 or robotaxi systems, including fail-operational and redundancy concepts.
• Experience with assisted driving (L0-L2+) functions and their system requirements.
• Experience with AI- or ML-based driving systems and their deployment on embedded platforms.
• Familiarity with automotive middleware, real-time operating systems, Linux and embedded platform integration.
• Experience with vehicle connectivity, remote assistance, remote operation / teleoperation, fleet operations, HMI or other robotaxi application-layer integration.
• Experience bridging internal product architecture and external customer integration.

title: Tacto Labs: Fast-Track Builder Program
description:
WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Manufacturing is Europe’s backbone, and it’s under pressure. More than half of manufacturing cost is decided in procurement, yet the function still runs on Excel.

Tacto's sales-led motion in DACH works: more than 300 industrial companies run on Tacto. Tacto Labs is where we build what comes nest: new products and wedges that don't scale linearly with headcount. Each bet starts on a whiteboard and either becomes a real business inside Tacto or gets killed fast.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Take a bet from idea to first paying users, working directly with our founders

- Build it yourself with AI: prototype, landing pages, agents, outreach, whatever proves or kills the idea fastest

- Talk to customers and suppliers until you know. more about the problem than anyone else in the company

- Find the next compounding loop and scale what works

 

HOW IT FITS

Everybody in Tacto Labs is a Builder: same role, same bar, pointed at earlier stage problems. We believe in building over strategizing.

 

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- You've built something from zero: as a founder, early at a startup, or during a side project.

- You want to found something someday. We're looking for people we'd back if they did.

- You don't come from engineering? Great, as long as you build. If you've shipped something with with AI tools, you're technical enough to start and get better.

- Extreme ownership, no ego.

- Fluent in German; English is a strong plus.

 

HOW THE PROCESS WORKS

1. Say Hello (20 min): get to know each other and the role

2. Hiring Manager Interview (45 min)

3. On-site day: a case with three Builders and Pool Leads (1 hour), Meet the Team (30 min)

HOW WE WORK

We’re in our Munich office four days a week, with 100+ people building together every day. We measure outcomes. Trust is high and feedback is direct. We offer competitive salary and meaningful equity.

OUR BACKGROUND

Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.

title: Business Operations Generalist, Finance & Accounting
description:
About Wonderly

Wonderly is a closed-loop, end-to-end system that self-improves on our customers’ revenue. We serve the home service industry ($1.3T), and can consistently double a new customer’s revenue within 90 days. We make all of our AI and software completely free - and only get paid when our customers make real money. We’re here helping real small businesses make a life, pay for their children’s college tuition, and live the American dream.

Pre-AI SaaS sold tools. AI companies claim they sell outcomes - task done, call answered, lead booked, ticket resolved - but calls or leads aren’t the outcomes that ultimately matter. Revenue is what ultimately matters, and today, none of the AI companies actually promise revenue. Wonderly changes that.

Our 70-person team (mostly in PDE) spent over a year building in stealth; our thesis is that - if you actually want to control the end result (revenue) of a business and deploy AI fast/cheaply, you can’t just build the sexy part (agents), you must also build the unsexy parts and own everything end to end: the system of record layer and the application layer. We built from scratch every software a home service business needs - replacing ServiceTitan, Squarespace, Ringcentral, Jobber, Square, Hubspot, and a dozen others applications. And we built every agent necessary - AI marketing, AI receptionist, AI voice, AI sales outreach, AI sales coaching, AI follow-ups, AI 3D design, AI finance, AI quoting, AI collections, and more - all embedded inside our own system with native data access. As a result, we can deploy dozens of production-ready Agents to our customers in under 24 hours with no FDEs, no integrations, and no data cleaning work.

We are the most outcome driven business model in the business because we’ve proven our system and AI Agents actually work in driving the end result - revenue. We are not trying to sell our customers a dream - each of our 10+ core AI Agents help improve our customers’ revenue by 5-20%.

The rest spans contracts, procurement, insurance, equity administration, and the operational problems that come with a growing company.
We want someone with an accounting foundation who wants broad business ownership. You should be comfortable investigating an unfamiliar charge, working through a vendor renewal, coordinating with outside counsel, and building a process so the same issue is easier next time.

Sundays for Dogs is a founder-led brand reimagining pet food so dog owners can spend more quality time with their dogs-now and later. We make human-grade, air-dried food that supports long, healthy lives, and we're building a company that reflects how great teams should work: with low ego, high ownership, honest feedback, creative problem-solving, and a bias toward doing more with less.

Headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, we're a distributed team of 70 full-time employees across the U.S. While we work remotely day-to-day, we gather quarterly in person because relationships matter. Our subscription-based DTC model is our foundation. We're entering an exciting growth stage-expanding our product assortment, driving innovation, and thoughtfully opening new channels. We're building to scale with intention, and we're just getting started.

About your team and position:

We're looking for a knowledgeable, detail-oriented Nutrition & Quality Specialist to join our Food Quality & Safety team at Sundays for Dogs .

In this role, you'll be the go-to expert for customers who have questions about our food, from ingredients and nutrition to product quality and safety. You'll use your veterinary background to translate complex scientific information into clear, accurate, and approachable answers that help pet parents feel confident about what they're feeding their dogs.

You'll work closely with our Customer Care team, serving as a technical resource for more complex inquiries while partnering with our Food Quality & Safety, R&D, and Veterinary teams to ensure we're delivering accurate, science-backed information.

This is a unique opportunity to apply your veterinary experience beyond the clinic, helping pet parents better understand the food they feed their dogs while directly contributing to the quality and safety of our products.

This is a fully-remote position with occasional trips to our headquarters in Cleveland, OH.

Your day-to-day:

Customer Education & Technical Support

• Serve as the primary point of contact for escalated customer inquiries related to canine nutrition, ingredients, food quality, and product safety.

• Explain nutritional concepts, ingredient functionality, feeding guidelines, and dietary transitions in a way that's accurate, approachable, and easy for pet parents to understand.

• Help customers navigate questions about food sensitivities, digestive concerns, and life-stage nutritional needs, recognizing when veterinary consultation is appropriate.

• Partner with Customer Care to resolve complex food-related inquiries via email, chat, and phone.

Food Quality & Safety

• Investigate and respond to customer concerns related to product quality, appearance, consistency, packaging, and food safety.

• Identify, document, and escalate potential product quality issues, adverse events, and safety concerns in accordance with established protocols.

• Collaborate with Food Quality & Safety and R&D to investigate customer-reported issues and provide accurate, timely responses.

• Maintain detailed records of customer inquiries, investigations, and resolutions.

• Identify trends in customer feedback that may signal opportunities to improve product quality, customer education, or internal processes.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Education

• Serve as a technical resource for the Customer Care team, helping them confidently navigate questions about our products.

• Partner with Food Quality & Safety, R&D, Veterinary, and Customer Care teams to ensure consistent, scientifically accurate communication.

• Help develop and maintain educational resources, FAQs, and internal training materials related to nutrition, ingredients, and food safety.

• Share recurring customer questions, concerns, and insights with relevant teams to continuously improve our products and customer experience.

•
First 30 Days: Complete onboarding on Sundays' products, ingredients, nutritional stand

description:
ABOUT US

Higharc is a VC-backed startup that is changing how new homes are designed and built. Join a founding team who’ve shipped products for Autodesk, Electronic Arts, Nike, and Apple. We have raised over $175M with support from top-notch venture capital firms and more than 18 strategic investors: industry leaders in construction, building products manufacturing, and distribution.

Higharc is seeking a hands-on Growth Lead to run the GTM experiment loop for our new self-serve business. This is a hybrid marketer and builder role: you’ll design tests against the self-serve funnel, build what’s needed to run them, interpret the results, and scale those that work.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Self-serve is a new business line at Higharc, and we’re placing bets in two parallel tracks, product and GTM. You’ll own the GTM experiment loop end to end. That means taking ideas from hypothesis to live test to a kill-or-scale decision fast.

You’ll build the landing pages, tooling, tracking, and automation each experiment needs, then judge the results with a sharp analytical eye. When something starts to feel magical, we shut down the weaker experiments and point more of the team at what’s working.

You’ll work closely with the Applications team and marketing, and both should see you as the fastest way to test an idea. The team works most often out of our Durham and NYC hubs.

Expect to:

- Design and run rapid growth and PLG experiments across acquisition, activation, and conversion in the self-serve funnel

- Build the landing pages, tooling, tracking, and automation needed to get each test live

- Instrument the self-serve funnel well enough to see where people drop off and why

- Interpret results and make fast kill-or-scale calls

- Document and share experiment results so the team builds real signal over time

- Move people and effort behind the experiments that work

- Partner closely with the Applications team and marketing to turn ideas into live tests quickly and iteratively

ABOUT YOU

You’re part marketer, part builder, and your marketing instinct matters as much as your technical ability. You care more about speed and learning than polish, you’re fine throwing away work that didn’t pan out, and you can work with limited direction in a brand-new business line.

You own outcomes, stay steady when things are ambiguous, and can tell real signal from noise.

You have:

- Experience shipping growth experiments end to end, ideally in a PLG or self-serve product

- Hands-on technical skills: you’re comfortable writing code and working with analytics, automation, and AI tooling

- Marketing instinct that carries as much weight as your technical ability

- Strong analytical judgment and the honesty to call a failed test a failure

- A preference for speed over polish

- Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to work with limited direction

- A strong sense of ownership over the work and its results

A major plus if you also bring:

title: Dutch Speaking Go Coding Evaluation Specialist
description:
Join a short, paid project that tests whether AI coding agents work as well on instructions written in the target language as they do in English. Your language skills and technical background decide where you fit.
About the project
Welo Data is helping evaluate how well AI coding agents perform when the instructions they receive are written in languages other than English. Agents are given a real software engineering task in a code repository, and automated tests check whether they solved it. The code, repositories and tests stay exactly as they are. Only the human-written instructions change language, so the quality of every instruction directly affects the result.
About the roles
There are two roles on this project. We place you in one of them based on your experience & skillsets.

• Translator: translate English software engineering task briefs into the target language. You keep every requirement, constraint and success condition, and you leave commands, file paths, API names, code and test conditions exactly as written in English. This role suits people with a stronger technical background, and translation experience is a plus.

• Reviewer: compare each translation with the English source, check that nothing is missing, added or changed in meaning, correct errors, and log each correction by error type. This role suits people with strong translation, editing or review experience and enough technical familiarity to read code context.

Who we are looking for

• Native or near-native writing in the target language, and strong reading ability in English.

• Either professional experience in translation, editing, review or technical writing, or a software background combined with excellent writing in the target language

• Comfort reading technical text. Coding experience is a strong plus for the translation role and helpful for the review role.

• Close attention to detail. In this project, a dropped clause can make a task fail.

Project at a glance

• Project duration: one week since the mid of November

• Languages: Dutch

• Project time commitment: 6 hours per person

• Project compensation: US$80-US$92.5 per hour

• Work location: fully remote

How selection works (major steps)

• Screening questions: about 2 minutes. They cover your language background, translation and review experience, which programming languages you know and how well, and your availability.

• Language test: short exercises in the target language.

• Programming skills assessment: you will be invited to another opportunity, in the programming language you know best (Rust, Go, Python, or TypeScript / JavaScript). It confirms your technical level and places you in a language track.

• Financial Onboarding & Role placement: complete the financial onboarding with Welo Data. In the meanwhile, you will be informed about the decision whether you are placed in the initial translation role or the review role.

• Production: once you finish all steps above, our project team will contact you for production.

title: Strategic Client Manager
description:
ABOUT FLOCK

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

Our largest fleet clients have the most vehicles, the most data and the most to gain from our connected proposition. As our Strategic Client Manager, you’ll be the main face of Flock for them, from multinationals and well-known brands to fast-growing sector leaders, and you’ll own those relationships end to end.

Nearly all our business comes through brokers, so you’ll sit at the centre of the client, broker and Flock relationship, working closely with our Broker Development Managers and teams across the business. You’ll build our corporate client management approach from scratch, from account reviews and performance reporting to bringing claims, safety, underwriting and finance together for our biggest clients. You’ll report to our Head of Distribution and use AI day to day to prepare for meetings, understand accounts and improve reporting. Success means our clients stay with us and recommend us to others.

 

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

- Own the relationship with a portfolio of Flock’s largest fleet clients, becoming their primary point of contact and developing a strong understanding of their business.

- Build and run our corporate account management approach: client reviews, reporting, relationship cadence and account planning.

- Work closely with brokers and our Broker Development Managers to deliver a coordinated experience for every large corporate client.

- Bring together teams across Flock, including claims, safety, underwriting and finance, to resolve client questions and issues quickly, and build strong relationships with key stakeholders across client organisations.

- Identify retention risks early and create clear plans to protect our most important accounts.

- Help shape and improve Flock’s wider client service proposition, including account reviews, portal engagement, safety support, claims and reporting, feeding client feedback back into the business.

- Use AI in your day-to-day work, from account research and meeting preparation to query management, meeting summaries and client reporting.

 

WHAT YOU’LL NEED

- Strong experience within the insurance industry, with a clear understanding of the broker-client-insurer dynamic and the judgement to know where you add value, without duplicating the broker’s role, creating confusion or adding unnecessary layers for the client.

- Experience in a client-facing role such as insurer account or deal management, broker account management, claims relationship management or a similar position.

- A proven track record of managing important client relationships and delivering strong retention or customer satisfaction, with the confidence to work with senior stakeholders across clients, brokers and internal teams.

- Strong commercial judgement. You can identify when an account is at risk, understand what matters to the client and build a plan to retain them.

- Energy and ownership. You’re comfortable picking up a problem, finding the right people and driving it through to a solution.

- Confident using technology in your daily work, curious about how it can help you work faster and deliver a better client experience.
